To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a three dimensional FEL theory in the high gain regime, including the effects of energy spread, emittance and betatron oscillations, that the theory is applicable to a wide range of electron beam distributions, that the theory can be applied directly to beam conditioning, that we have derived an interpolating formula for gain as a function of scaled parameters, and that the present theory can be easily applied to the case of a helical wiggler and to other types of FEL devices.

the three-dimensional small-signal FEL theory based upon the Maxwell- Vlasov equations is developed, including the effects of energy spread, emittance, and betatron oscillations, the theory is applicable to the beam-condition case, and the theory is compared with simulation and other analytical approaches.
the three-dimensional FEL gain is significantly reduced from that predicted in a one-dimensional model, and that the FEL gain is a function of the electron-beam emittance and the betatron wavelength.
